newsitem.title: USA: Murphy to withdraw from proposed merger.
newsitem.headline: Murphy to withdraw from proposed merger.

text.p: Murphy Oil Corp said Thursday it withdrew from the proposed merger of the U.K. refining and marketing interests of its wholly owned subsidiary, Murco Petroleum Ltd.

Murco was to merge U.K. refining and marketing operations with those of Elf Oil U.K. Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Elf Aquitaine of France, and Gulf Oil (Great Britain) Ltd., a wholly owned subsidiary of Chevron Corp.

Claiborne P. Deming, President and Chief Executive Officer of Murphy, said in a statement: "Our analysis of the proposed transaction indicated that the advantages of scale of the newly merged company would not significantly improve Murphy's existing, cost-effective and efficient downstream system.
Deming said that Murphy can better achieve its goals in the U.K. through continued rationalization of its existing low-cost retail marketing network and refining assets.
"Efforts will be focused on developing a niche, leading-edge company; however, mergers or joint ventures with other companies will be evaluated as part of this strategy," he said.

"Murphy recognizes the need to continue to optimize its business plan and asset utilization to prosper in the rapidly restructuring U.K. market. The strategy has not changed, only the tactics," he said.

Mr. Deming added: "Each party's situation is different and that means different factors and views are brought to bear on the same structure. We, of course, speak only for Murphy, and wish Elf and Gulf every success."
The U.K. refining industry has suffered in recent years from a surplus capacity for gasoline production and the worldwide refinery glut.

The downstream industry also has suffered from a national price war among gasoline retailers, initiated at the start of last year by Esso U.K., an Exxon Corp, subsidiary, in response to rapid growth of supermarkets as gasoline retailers.
